judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The page is a news article whose h1 (live HTML, and visible in the screenshot) reads 'Irish father says work colleague saved his life after stroke left him speaking gibberish', and whose body tells how Kieran O'Carroll's co-worker got him to hospital during a stroke. The title 'Irish father says colleague saved his life after stroke' is a condensed form of that headline, so it describes the page's topic and purpose and 2.4.2 is met. The snapshot hit its 5000-element limit (truncated: true) inside the Cookiebot consent dialog, whose cookie detail tables fill the whole tree; no article node was collected, h1 is reported empty, and the content text the model saw was only the consent dialog. The model compared the title with the cookie banner, not with the article.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the img #CybotCookiebotDialogPoweredbyImage in the visible Cookiebot consent dialog; the crop and screenshot show it is the 'IrishCentral.' wordmark, and its HTML has alt="logo". I looked for a reason it could pass: it is not hidden from assistive technology (no aria-hidden, the dialog is shown), it is not inside a link or next to text that names IrishCentral (its parent is a plain div, and the dialog text says only 'We and our 1090 partners'), and 'logo' is Cookiebot's generic default alt rather than an author-written alternative. As an informative image of text it needs an alternative such as 'IrishCentral'; 'logo' names the kind of image, not its content, which is the placeholder pattern of failure F30. Even if one treated the logo as decorative, a non-empty alt keeps it from being ignored (F38), so the image fails 1.1.1 either way. The dialog is injected by script, so curl of the live page cannot recheck it, but the DOM attribute in the snapshot is direct evidence.
